stories.title: Kerala Literature Festival promises much for book lovers as it returns after pandemic
stories.summary: Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan to open the event on Kozhikode beach on Thursday
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once

article_sentences: It has not taken the Kerala Literature Festival (KLF) long to earn a prominent place in the State’s cultural landscape.
After a three-year break, necessitated by the pandemic, the KLF is back in the physical world (it was held online in 2021).
The sixth edition will get under way on the Kozhikode beach on Thursday.
It promises plenty for the book lovers of Malabar and beyond over the next four years.

Writers such as Shehan Karunatilaka, who won the Booker Prize three months ago, Arundhati Roy, Shashi Tharoor, Nobel laureates Ada Yonath and Abhijit Banerjee, historians William Dalrymple, Yuval Noah Harari, Ramachandra Guha, Manu S. Pillai, actors Kamal Haasan, Prakash Raj, Mukesh, and Indrans are among those who will speak at sessions that will deal with a variety of topics.
Around 500 speakers, including those from countries such as the United States, UK, Spain, Israel, and New Zealand, will speak in 248 sessions, in fact.
“This is going to be the biggest edition of the KFL yet,” the festival’s chief facilitator.
Ravi Deecee told The Hindu.
“In 2020, the footfall for the festival was around three lakh.
We expect that number to go up to four or five lakh this time,” he added.
He said he was glad that the festival had evolved as something that was not just literature.
“For instance, we have been able to line up several prominent economists this time around.

stories.headline: India's ties with Russia an 'added value', can help push for end to Ukraine war: Dutch FM
stories.title: India's ties with Russia an 'added value', can help push for end to Ukraine war: Dutch FM
stories.summary: India and the Netherlands, as trading countries, share concerns over maritime security and freedom of navigation, and needed to work together to address challenges in an increasingly uncertain world
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Netherlands sees India's continued engagement with Russia as an "added value," as it believes New Delhi can use its ties with Moscow to persuade it to end the Ukraine war, Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said on Sunday.
Berendsen is on an official visit to India from November 22 to 23.
He co-chaired the inaugural Foreign Ministers' Meeting with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi on Sunday and reviewed the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership.

"We understand that India has its own history, its own role in the world and its own relations," Berendsen told PTI, responding to a question on India's strategic autonomy and its continued engagement with Moscow.

"We actually see it as an added value of our relationship with India that it has a relationship with Russia and can also use that relation to show Russia that it needs to put an end to this war and accept a ceasefire," he said.
The Russia-Ukraine war, in its fifth year, continues with intensified attacks from both sides.
Russia has stepped up strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, while US-brokered peace talks have made little progress beyond a prisoner swap.

Berendsen said India and the Netherlands, as trading countries, shared concerns over maritime security and freedom of navigation, and needed to work together to address challenges in an increasingly uncertain world.
"I think we're dealing with the same challenges: how to decrease dependencies, how to be more strategically autonomous on critical raw materials, technology and energy," he said.
"If you want to do that, you need to diversify, which means new partnerships.
I think the Netherlands, the EU and India are doing exactly that," he added.
On trade, he described the proposed India-European Union free trade agreement, expected to be signed in December, as a crucial step that could open opportunities beyond merchandise trade.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan disrupts fishing in Tamil Nadu's Tuticorin; fishermen seek Rs 5,000 assistance
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan disrupts fishing in Tamil Nadu's Tuticorin; fishermen seek Rs 5,000 assistance
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu): Over 200 mechanised fishing boats from Tuticorin ventured into the sea early on Monday after a 10-day break triggered by Cyclone Akvan, even as fishermen urged the Tamil Nadu government to provide Rs 5,000 in relief to tide over the monsoon-induced lean period.
Following an India Meteorological Department warning of strong winds over the sea due to Cyclone Akvan, the Tuticorin district.
Fisheries Department had barred fishermen from venturing into the waters from November 13 until further notice.
After the restriction was lifted, country-boat and fibre-boat fishermen resumed operations on November 20.
Mechanised boat operators, however, remained ashore for 10 days before setting sail early Monday from the Tuticorin Mechanised Boat Fishing Harbour.
With fishing resuming after a 10-day gap, fishermen expressed optimism that the catch would be good.
Highlighting the recurring impact of the northeast monsoon, fishermen noted that rough seas and cyclonic systems between October and December steadily reduce their working days every year.
In November alone, they were forced to stay off the sea for 17 days, severely affecting their livelihoods.

Fishermen urged the state government to enhance the financial assistance extended during the May fishing ban and lean fishing periods, and provide an additional Rs 5,000 to cover the three-month monsoon lean season.

A fishermen's representative told PTI Videos that it has become extremely difficult to venture into the sea even for 150 days out of 365 in a year, given cyclones, floods, and the mandatory 60-day annual fishing ban.

Urging the government to intervene and hike the relief amount this year itself, the representative sought an immediate allocation of Rs 5,000 for the November–December period to support families facing severe hardship.
Tuticorin is a major fishing harbour, with over 20,000 people depending directly on the sector and another 10,000 indirectly for their livelihoods.

stories.headline: TCS, Infosys, Wipro, other IT stocks rise up to 3% as AI bloodbath continues; Nasdaq logs worst week since 2020
stories.title: TCS, Infosys, Wipro, other IT stocks rise up to 3% as AI bloodbath continues; Nasdaq logs worst week since 2020
stories.summary: Shares of information technology companies such as TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Tech Mahindra and HCL Tech rallied up to 3% on Monday, even as an AI-linked selloff continued to rattle investor sentiment across the US and Asia. In the US, Nvidia, AMD and Micron shares crashed up to 14% each, while Meta, Google and Amazon fell up to 6%.In today’s session, Wipro and TCS shares gained 2% and 3% respectively, while Infosys, HCL Tech and Tech Mahindra gained 2.5%, 2% and 3%, respectively. Midcap IT stocks Coforge and Persistent Systems gained 2.5% and 2%, respectively. The Nifty IT index rose over 700 points to a high of 32,034.AI-rout DeepensInvestors are increasingly questioning whether the massive sums, largely financed through borrowing, being poured into data centres to power artificial intelligence tools will generate returns quickly enough to repay lenders or justify the lofty valuations of some technology stocks.South Korean equities tumbled on Monday, as government assurances of market support failed to calm investor concerns over the AI trade and a broader technology selloff.Also Read: S&P 500 plunges into correction mode, Nasdaq crashes: Why are Wall Street stocks down on Friday?The benchmark KOSPI plunged more than 3%, hovering near its lowest level since January. The decline came despite authorities announcing on Sunday that market stabilisation funds would be deployed immediately if conditions deteriorated further. The assurance followed a sharp selloff last week that had dragged the index to a 10-month low.Shares of major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell around 4% each, extending pressure on the region's technology stocks.The weakness follows a bruising week for global equities. The Nasdaq lost 10% last week, marking its biggest weekly decline since the pandemic-driven market panic in March 2020. Taiwan's benchmark index also recorded its steepest weekly fall since 1990. Taiwan is home to the world's leading advanced chipmakers and remains a crucial part of the global AI supply chain.AI-linked stocks came under particularly heavy selling pressure last week. The exit of Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive often described as the "godfather of AI", and the disappointing market debut of AI company Anthropic added to the increasingly cautious mood. Anthropic shares ended 8.5% lower on their first full day of trading.Governments and regulators across the region have also moved to contain market volatility. Taiwan's financial regulator on Saturday ordered further restrictions on short-selling in stocks, while Chinese stock exchanges announced a series of support measures, including relaxed requirements for margin financing.Is IT out of the woods?Global brokerage Jefferies picks Coforge and Sagility as their top picks. Analysts said growth improved, and net hiring picked up, but soft deal bookings and rising subcontractor usage suggest limited confidence in sustained growth. “AI services are gaining traction, but weakness in non-AI and Hi-Tech verticals suggests that the sector is not out of the woods yet. Rising competition and INR appreciation also pose risks to margins,” the brokerage said in a note.Jefferies said HCLTech, Wipro and Tech Mahindra surprised positively on revenue growth in its coverage universe, while Hexaware Technologies delivered a negative surprise. Aggregate operating margins expanded 25 basis points sequentially to 19.9%, led by a 130-basis-point expansion at HCLTech, 45 basis points at Wipro and 35 basis points at TechM. Margins at other IT companies remained largely flat quarter-on-quarter.Read more: NSE becomes world’s 5th-largest listed stock exchange, surpasses NASDAQ and HKEXThe brokerage also flagged a steady rise in subcontracting costs even as employee costs as a share of sales continued to decline over recent quarters. The divergence suggests lower confidence among IT companies about the growth outlook, Jefferies said.Jefferies is bearish on TCS, HCL Tech, Wipro, and Tech Mahindra, assigning an Underperform rating to all.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. stories.headline: PM Modi's Gold Appeal: Foreign Exchange Savings, Gold Prices & Congress-Shastri Row
stories.title: PM Modi's Gold Appeal: Foreign Exchange Savings, Gold Prices & Congress-Shastri Row
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has credited citizens for responding to his appeal to avoid unnecessary gold purchases, as gold prices take a dip. Speaking at the National Skill Convocation in Lucknow, the PM said public cooperation could help conserve India's foreign exchange reserves amid global economic and energy uncertainties. The appeal, first made in Hyderabad in May, has also received backing from traders' bodies and Union Minister Piyush Goyal. But Modi's comparison with former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri's appeal to give up one meal a week during the 1965 war has triggered a political controversy, with Congress MP Imran Masood questioning the comparison. Did the appeal help India's economy, or has it become another political flashpoint?

stories.headline: 228 GW Solar, 135.8 GWh BESS Pipeline Raise Credit & Execution Risks: Study
stories.title: 228 GW Solar, 135.8 GWh BESS Pipeline Raise Credit & Execution Risks: Study
stories.summary: Two recent reports by India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) and CareEdge highlight widening credit divergence among domestic solar module manufacturers amid an increasing shift towards BESS manufacturing and rising operational capacity. Demand for BESS is rising as renewable energy additions outpace transmission infrastructure development. A recent ICRA report emphasises that execution is a key monitorable in building Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity amid growing storage demand and with enlarging tender pipeline. This trend is particularly acute in resource-rich states such as Rajasthan and Gujarat. This, in turn, is creating grid congestion and a growing need for storage to absorb surplus generation, shift supply to non-solar hours, and ease network constraints. IndiRa special report, “Policy Access, Integration, and ROCE Will Drive Credit for Solar Module Manufacturers”, examines domestic manufacturing economics, ALMM-II and DCR implications, margin migration, technology and execution risks, BESS diversification, and the likely rating outlook for the sector. Emphasising on the impact on the BESS project, the research noted, a shift in Indian BESS market from tendering to execution, backed by policy support and a large tender pipeline. However, the rebound in battery prices, rupee depreciation and aggressive bids make timely battery procurement, robust LTSAs and offtake tie-ups critical for project viability. Credit Divergence & Solar Cell Import Dependence Affect the Indian Market Another key element is credit considerations, which are now emerging as an important factor requiring attention. Credit divergence across domestic solar module manufacturers is emerging in FY27, even as strong solar power demand continues, indicating widening differences in manufacturers' credit profiles. However, import dependence continues, with imported-cell modules being 3-4 US cents/W cheaper than domestic-content-requirement modules, even after basic customs duty. Consequently, the implementation of the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) List-II will be central to absorbing domestic cell capacity. The divergence is unfolding against a backdrop of stable module capacity at 228 GW, which is more than three times the estimated annual requirement of 65-70 GW. This makes capacity utilisation, technology relevance, customer access, liquidity, and returns on capital more important than announced capacity alone. Solar to Push for Further Upstream Manufacturing From Modules to Cells and Ingots Ind-Ra marks the shift in Indian solar sector with the change in its margin pool from modules to cells. With margins likely to move further upstream towards ingots and wafers as backward integration gathers pace, its expected to favour well-capitalised integrated manufacturers. However, substantially higher capex, technology, commissioning, power, and refinancing risks will increase rating sensitivity. Therefore, the winners according to the report would be those who can provider low-debt module manufacturers with strong channels and high asset turns. This may remain viable at lower margins, while leveraged greenfield projects and standalone assemblers dependent on spot cells will be more exposed as domestic cell spreads normalise. “Policy access and integration will increasingly determine market position, but neither guarantees stronger credit quality. As manufacturers move upstream, the ability to preserve return on capital, manage technology transitions, and fund expansion without weakening liquidity will separate sustainable business models from capacity-led growth,” says Bhanu Patni, Director, Corporate Ratings, Ind-Ra. BESS Pack Costs Remain Central to Assessment At a battery pack cost of USD 70/kWh, a cumulative DSCR of 1.17-1.27 times is expected at tariffs of Rs. 2.60-2.80 lakh/MW/month. Competitive procurement and protection against cost escalation remain central to the assessment. Operational BESS capacity is also rising, signalling progress from tendering to deployment. Policy support, including the Government of India’s VGF schemes announced in 2023, 2025, and 2026, covering 135.8 GWh, provides a significant source of capital support. Battery procurement costs and currency movements remain critical to the viability of aggressively bid projects. ICRA’s sensitivity analysis highlights limited coverage headroom at lower capacity tariffs. Merchant BESS Viability: Arbitrage Margins Need Adequate Utilisation Sustained arbitrage margins and adequate utilisation are critical to merchant BESS viability. ICRA’s analysis indicates a cumulative DSCR of 1.35-1.52 times at a charging cost of Rs. 2/unit and discharge realisation of Rs. 6.0-6.5/unit, under the stated assumptions. Narrowing peak-off-peak spreads, fewer viable trading cycles, lower efficiency, and availability shortfalls remain key risks to cash flows and debt coverage, necessitating adequate liquidity buffers. Lower upfront funding and supplier guarantees do not eliminate future costs and operating risks. Project assessments should account for eventual duty payments under MOOWR and check whether supplier guarantees adequately cover commitments to the power buyer. Costs not covered by the supplier, including performance penalties, additional batteries, and post-warranty maintenance, remain important risks for the developer.

stories.headline: Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on PIL for reforms in anti-defection law
stories.title: Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on PIL for reforms in anti-defection law
stories.summary: The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) sought responses from the Centre, the Election Commission of India and the Law Commission on a PIL seeking comprehensive reforms in the anti-defection framework.
The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments.

Besides the Election Commission and the law panel, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also issued notices to the Ministries of Law and Justice and Parliamentary Affairs on the PIL filed by A. Sethu.

The PIL, filed through lawyers R. Satish Kumar and Jatin, sought directions to prevent misuse of “strategic resignations” by MPs and lawmakers from legislative assemblies to evade discipline of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution.

It also sought directions to “(ii) secure time-bound, reasoned and transparent adjudication of resignations and disqualification proceedings; (iii) secure institutional review of the Speaker-centred adjudicatory mechanism; and (iv) reaffirm that in a hung Legislative Assembly, majority to form the Government must be tested only on the floor of a duly constituted House after Members are sworn under Article 188, and not through extra-parliamentary letters of support or demonstrations.”
The plea said that legislators facing, or anticipating, disqualification proceedings frequently resort to strategic resignations before the Speaker or Chairman can decide the cases on merit.

The plea said such resignations can be used to facilitate political realignments, alter the numerical strength of legislative assemblies and potentially enable elected representatives to evade the consequences contemplated under the anti-defection law.

“Declare and direct that a resignation tendered by a Member of Parliament or a Member of a State Legislative Assembly, at a stage when disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution are pending or reasonably imminent against such member, shall not ipso facto terminate or render infructuous such disqualification proceedings, and that the Speaker/Chairman shall record a reasoned order, based on objective material, on both the voluntariness and genuineness of the resignation and on the disqualification petition,” the plea said.

The plea sought direction to Speakers and Chairpersons to examine the voluntariness and genuineness of resignations on the basis of objective material and pass reasoned orders, while ensuring that pending disqualification proceedings are independently adjudicated.

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(November 23) suspended the sentence of Irfan Siraj Pada, one of the convicts in the Godhra train burning case.
It granted bail to him on medical grounds and considering that he has been in custody for more than 17 years.
A bench comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale passed an order considering that Irfan suffers from serious cardiovascular disease.
The State did not dispute the medical condition of the convict.
The crime which took place on February 27, 2002, resulted in the killing of 58 persons in a fire inside the S-6 coach of the Sabarmati Express, which was carrying kar sevaks from Ayodhya.
The Godhra carnage triggered communal riots in Gujarat.
In March 2011, the trial court had convicted 31 persons, of whom 11 were sentenced to death and the remaining 20 awarded life in prison.
63 other accused were acquitted.
In 2017, the Gujarat High Court commuted the death sentence of 11 to life-term and upheld the life sentence awarded to the other 20.
The appeals filed by the convicts in the Supreme Court have been pending since 2018.

On May 13, 2022, the Court had granted one of the convicts, Abdul Raheman Dhantiya @ Kankatto @Jamburo, interim bail for six months on the ground that his wife was suffering from terminal cancer and that his daughters were mentally challenged.
On November 11, 2022, the Court extended his bail till March 31, 2023.

stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses PIL Seeking Corrections In UP Municipal Electoral Rolls
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a public interest litigation (PIL) that sought corrections to municipal electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh over alleged discrepancies in house numbers.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana declined to entertain the plea.
Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed that the right to seek correction of an electoral-roll entry is personal to the individual voter and cannot ordinarily be pursued collectively through a PIL.
“You are moving this petition as a public interest litigation.
The right to correct an electoral roll is personal.
In your municipal list also, there will be certain rules.
Let the individuals approach.
But on a collective basis, it can only be when it is done across the State.
Voters can take it up.
Individual voters can come to us,” Justice Bagchi said.
The Court noted that municipal electoral rolls are governed by their own set of rules and that individual voters can approach the competent election authorities for necessary corrections.

The petitioner had contended that house numbers had changed in several areas, that representations made in this regard remained unaddressed, and that municipal electoral rolls should be aligned with those prepared for parliamentary and assembly elections.

article_sentences: Indore Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri has said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s policies insulated Indian consumers from global fuel price shocks, underscoring that domestic retail prices remained largely stable despite international crises.

Inspecting petrol pumps in Indore on Sunday, the Rajya Sabha member from Madhya Pradesh said the Centre had cut excise duty three times, in November 2021, May 2022 and March 10, 2026, limiting the rise in fuel prices in India to "around seven per cent against a 50-70 per cent surge globally".
PM Modi's policies protected Indians from global fuel price shocks, he told reporters.

He also praised state-run oil marketing companies Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) for "absorbing heavy losses" when crude oil prices rose from $60-65 to $120 per barrel.
Dismissing the Opposition's claims about shortage of petrol, diesel and cooking gas amid the Iran conflict as baseless rumours, the minister said supplies remained uninterrupted across the country.
"Not a single one of our 1,07,000 retail outlets experienced a dry-out.
During the last Parliament session, our political friends welcomed me with gas cylinder cutouts, claiming an imminent crisis and that LPG cylinders had run out.
"Yet, there was no shortage anywhere because we ramped up domestic LPG production," he said.
